metadata.title: EyeDataHub first-release literature and repository discovery audit
metadata.interpretation: This decision log documents the searches and curation audit used to assemble EyeDataHub and the literature refresh completed through 21 July 2026. The 209-record working count was an internal curation state, not an earlier release. Three records were removed after their official acquisition routes could not be confirmed. One current combined CORN collection record supplied by the authors was added on 25 July 2026 and linked to its overlapping component records. Publicly discoverable means that a documented open, account-based, competition, request, or data-use route exists; it does not imply unrestricted download or reuse.

include: Eye- or ophthalmology-related data with a stable public landing page and documented access route.
A reusable dataset, benchmark, annotation layer, or analysis-ready cohort rather than an article-only claim or ordinary figure source-data deposit.
At least one plausible machine-learning, statistical, measurement, or evaluation task.
Enough source metadata to record provenance, access, and conservative license text.
eligibility.derived_resource_rule: Retain a composite, synthetic, or derived resource only when it adds a distinct annotation, representation, longitudinal target, benchmark, or access surface; state known upstream dependencies in notes.
eligibility.license_rule: Use repository or dataset terms, not the article license. Mark unclear or mixed terms as unknown and require source verification.

searches.interface: REST search API plus primary-paper and data-availability verification
searches.query: (TITLE:"dataset" OR ABSTRACT:"public dataset" OR ABSTRACT:"publicly available dataset") AND (ophthalmology OR ophthalmic OR retina OR retinal OR ocular OR cornea OR fundus OR "optical coherence tomography") AND FIRST_PDATE:[2024-01-01 TO 2026-12-31]
searches.purpose: Identify recent dataset papers missed by platform-only searches.

searches.screening_note: All 219 unique titles were inspected. Ten clearly reusable clinical, imaging, omics, or ML-oriented resources were selected for full repository-metadata verification during the audit for the first release. The remaining records include basic-science experiment deposits, non-ophthalmic visual-neuroscience false positives, article source data, code-only deposits, and potentially eligible resources that still require full adjudication; they are not represented as definitively excluded.

searches.purpose: Verify current access routes, repository licenses, file sizes, sample units, and derivative status.

searches.source: Major gaze, pupil, and iris benchmark sweep
searches.screening_note: This targeted sentinel search was prompted by the registry's absence of iris-biometrics records and near-absence of eye-tracking records. It was intended to identify major benchmark families but was not a systematic review of all gaze or biometric-eye datasets. Candidates without a current primary access route or without completed source and license adjudication remain listed below.

not_included.reason: The paper says the dataset will be made public, but the working Figshare URL is still explicitly marked as a private share link; the claimed public article DOI returned no public API record on the search date.
The manuscript describes a 1,200-sample tri-modal glaucoma dataset, but no stable public download, request, or repository route was found.
The linked public repository exposed only example images during verification, not the complete dataset described by the paper.

LMOD+ provides the documented downloadable successor, expands the original benchmark by about 50 percent, and preserves a distinct public access route; counting both would add avoidable derivative duplication.

The primary papers document request-based release pages, but all tested Meta/Facebook Research dataset URLs now redirect to the generic Research homepage. Stable papers alone are not a current data-access route.

not_included.candidate: Additional gaze benchmarks (CAVE/Columbia Gaze, EYEDIAP, TabletGaze, UT Multiview, RT-GENE, EVE, NVGaze, SynthesEyes, and UnityEyes)
not_included.reason: These established candidates were identified during the bounded sentinel sweep but were not promoted without completing one-by-one primary-source, current-access, overlap, sample-unit, and license verification.
not_included.evidence: Candidate family retained for the next systematic gaze-dataset pass

not_included.candidate: Additional iris and periocular benchmarks (IITD, MICHE-I, UPOL, MMU, Warsaw BioBase, and LivDet-Iris)
not_included.reason: These candidates require one-by-one confirmation of a current owner-controlled access route, version boundaries, and dataset-specific reuse terms before registry inclusion.
not_included.evidence: Candidate family retained for the next systematic iris-dataset pass
